speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how will the Government tackle marine plastic pollution in the region; (b) what steps are being taken to prolong the life of Semakau landfill beyond 2035 by reducing excessive consumption of single-use plastic; and (c) how is the Government encouraging the private sector to develop, use and promote sustainable alternatives to plastic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources what plans does the Ministry have to encourage more businesses to reduce usage of single-use plastic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: My Ministry takes the issue of marine plastic pollution seriously, and measures are in place to prevent marine pollution from land-based sources.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, we have strict anti-littering measures and dispose of all general waste at our waste-to-energy plants.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Any litter that enters our waterways is removed using litter traps and flotsam removal craft before it reaches the sea.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, tackling marine plastic pollution will require international and regional cooperation because of its transboundary nature.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14 emphasises the conservation and sustainable use of the oceans, seas and marine resources.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Singapore actively participates in regional and global discussions to address marine litter and microplastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Singapore also contributes to international capacity building efforts under the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last October, the National Environment Agency (NEA) organised a joint Third Country Training Programme with Norway on waste management and reduction of marine litter for government officials from our region.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Waste, including single-use plastics, are already incinerated where possible as this reduces the volume of waste by up to 90%.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, they consume water during production or they result in forest destruction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Substituting plastics with these alternatives is not likely to improve the environmental outcome.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is especially so in Singapore where we incinerate our waste instead of landfilling it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our approach, thus, is focused on reducing the use of single-use plastics and packaging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA provides funding support to organisations with initiatives to reduce the use of single-use disposables or promote plastic recycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These include the 3R Fund, 3P Partnership Fund or the Call for Ideas Fund.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, Zero Waste SG received funding for their Bring-Your-Own Campaign in 2017, where they partnered retailers to encourage consumers to use reusable containers, bottles and bags through educational tips, resources and incentives.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to engage, educate and support businesses and the public in reducing the use of single-use plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The private sector has also taken steps to discourage the excessive consumption of single-use plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) has stopped providing plastic lids and straws for dine-in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Startups like UnPackt are also promoting packaging-free shopping by requiring customers to bring their own reusable containers for groceries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To support R&D in waste reduction, recycling and the recovery of valuable fractions, NEA has embarked on the Closing the Waste Loop Initiative.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Initiative encourages collaboration between institutes of higher learning, research institutes and private sector partners to develop technologies and solutions to tackle challenges in waste management.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of the Initiative, NEA has solicited and is evaluating research proposals on the sustainable design of plastic materials, reducing the use of plastic materials and packaging, making plastics more reusable and easier to recycle, and recovering value from waste plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ultimately, the issue of marine plastic litter and excessive use of single-use plastics will require everyone to play his or her part.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This can be done by properly disposing of waste into litter bins and using reusable bags and containers, instead of disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Individuals can find information on other ways to reduce and reuse on our NEA website and the myENV mobile app.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask whether we will consider providing some incentives to these businesses or companies that are promoting environmentally friendly practices, such as the companies that are not giving out straws and plastic lids or even the packaging-free companies that the Senior Minister of State had mentioned?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second is on the plastic bag charge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know that, on the ground, one of the concerns is how do we reuse plastic bags when they were used to contain frozen food or meat and seafood.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, can the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) consider a selective plastic bag charge so that if you are using it not for frozen food, meat or seafood, then there will be a charge involved?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the first question relating to giving incentives to companies, as I have alluded to, we do provide support to companies that have initiatives to promote recycling, reduce the use of single use plastics and waste minimisation projects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, an example would be the 3R Fund, which I have talked about that was launched in 2009.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are also other incentives to acknowledge companies who have put in effort to reduce packaging waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also have the 3R awards for hotels and shopping malls to recognise their achievements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there are other funds like the Call for Ideas Fund and the 3P Partnership Fund.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to see and look into ways to support companies which promote waste minimisation and help us in our efforts to achieve a Zero Waste vision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the second question about plastic bag charge, as I have said earlier, the NEA lifecycle assessment study has shown that different types of disposables, whether it is single-use plastics or other types of bags, have an impact and cost on the environment, even biodegradable bags, because you need lots of water for production, for instance, or there will be forest destruction and greenhouse gas emissions in the process.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are really looking at is how we can do this in a holistic manner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, a city like San Francisco, for instance, is now imposing a charge not just on single-use plastic bags, but all kinds of disposable bags, paper as well as plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are monitoring this closely to see the effectiveness of the policy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, what is important is, we need to look at our local context, to adopt a rational and discerning approach to design policies suited to our unique needs and circumstances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, many of us stay in high-rise apartments and we use plastic bags to bag and dispose of our garbage.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It has taken us many years from the 1970s to get Singaporeans to do this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is a key way for hygienic disposal of waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to carefully consider how imposing a mandatory charge on single-use plastics will impact on such behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have a safe and efficient waste management and disposal system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All our plastic bags that are disposed properly will be incinerated.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They do not go directly into the landfill.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even for those that may get into our waterways, we have measures in place – litter traps, for instance, and flotsam removal craft – to retrieve these bags before they go into the sea.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding this, we recognise that plastic waste is a key waste stream.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Can I just ask a follow-up question, please?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate that the Ministry is looking at both taxes and incentives.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: And we know that there are some incentives for the companies that are doing the right thing.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned KFC as an example, and they have a "no straw" policy.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Can I ask: would the Government Ministries and agencies be encouraged not to use single-use plastics for all the catering, for all the events that happen?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be something that could be introduced or encouraged within the Government, in the public-private partnerships?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Certainly, this is something that we ought to consider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, I think what we want to do is to adopt a holistic approach and to tackle this upstream.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, by bringing forward the mandatory reporting of packaging waste and waste reduction plans, we are working on addressing the issue of excessive consumption of disposables, not just plastics, but all kinds of disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we will continue to monitor the effectiveness of various policies that are implemented overseas.
